scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8878: Users in both pods report the "web2.local" portal
returns nothing -- connections fail immediately instead of loading. The other
portals (web0/web1/web3) load fine. DNS resolves web2.local to 10.200.0.5,
and ping to 10.200.0.5 works from user machines. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_2

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: web_server_2 Apache (apache2) HTTP service
Mechanism: the apache2 service on web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) is stopped, so
  nothing listens on TCP/80 and connection attempts are refused immediately.
  Everything below the service layer is healthy: DNS still resolves
  web2.local -> 10.200.0.5, the OSPF path delivers packets (ping succeeds),
  and the other three web servers keep serving. The symptom is purely the
  dead HTTP daemon on one server.
Localization: web_server_2
Root cause: apache2 not running on web_server_2 (TCP/80 closed)
Fix: `service apache2 start` on web_server_2
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_2 (e.g. `service apache2 start`
/ `systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache listens on port 80 again,
http://web2.local serves normally. Nothing else needs changing.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-dns-and-network: notes DNS resolves web2.local correctly and 10.200.0.5 is reachable at the IP layer, ruling out name resolution and the network path

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is the Apache2 HTTP daemon on web_server_2 being dead — killed
by SIGTERM approximately 92 seconds after lab startup and never restarted.

Affected component: The Apache2 web server process (application layer /
HTTP daemon) on web_server_2 (10.200.0.5).

Mechanism: The Linux kernel handles ICMP echo (ping) entirely in kernel
space without any user-space daemon, so pings to 10.200.0.5 succeed
normally — L3 forwarding and IP addressing are intact. However, TCP
connections to port 80 require a listening process; with no process bound
to any TCP port (confirmed by netstat showing only Docker's internal DNS
at 127.0.0.11), every inbound SYN receives an immediate RST/ICMP
port-unreachable, which manifests as an instant connection failure.
DNS resolution is also correct and unaffected.

Localization: web_server_2 exclusively. The Apache2 error log records a
clean start at 04:41:19 ("resuming normal operations") followed by
"caught SIGTERM, shutting down" at 04:42:51. No apache2 or any other
HTTP server process appears in ps output. web_server_1 (and implicitly
web_server_0/3) show three apache2 worker processes and port 80 LISTEN.
The VirtualHost and ports.conf on web_server_2 are byte-for-byte
identical to web_server_1, ruling out misconfiguration.

Root cause: The lab's fault-injection mechanism delivered SIGTERM to the
apache2 master process on web_server_2 after startup; because Kathara
containers use plain bash as PID 1 (no systemd supervisor), the daemon
was not respawned and port 80 has been unbound ever since.

Corrective fix: On web_server_2, run `/usr/sbin/apache2 -k start` (or
`apache2ctl start`) to restore the daemon. For persistence across
restarts, ensure the .startup script launches apache2 and that no
background kill is injected after it.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) as the affected device throughout.
The report explicitly identifies that the apache2 HTTP daemon on web_server_2 is dead and that nothing is listening on TCP/80, recommending restarting the service.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-dns-and-network: notes DNS resolves web2.local correctly and 10.200.0.5 is reachable at the IP layer, ruling out name resolution and the network path
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states DNS resolves correctly and that pings to 10.200.0.5 succeed, thereby ruling out name resolution and network-path issues.
Proposes starting the Apache daemon on web_server_2 (apache2 -k start / apache2ctl start), which matches the expected restart-based fix.

The agent's investigation log contains strong, specific observations (netstat, ps, curl, ping, apache2ctl, and the apache error log showing a start then SIGTERM) that directly support the conclusion that apache2 on web_server_2 stopped and port 80 is closed; a few minor explanatory statements (e.g., exact byte-for-byte identity and the lab as the SIGTERM source) are slightly more speculative but do not undermine the core diagnosis.
